features.title: Research: the real uid of a socket peer under PrivateUsers=, and the D-Bus handshake on the socket
features.description: docs/findings/F170.md settles the open question 'The real uid under PrivateUsers=' (SPEC Design 1, 'Real uid' and 'Authentication handshake'). It measures, with a socket-activated test socket under a copy of the shipped unit (DynamicUser, PrivateUsers=), what SO_PEERCRED reports for a peer of another uid (the overflow uid 65534 or the real one), and compares the candidates: a PrivateUsers= mode that keeps uids identical (systemd 257 is the floor), another kernel-guaranteed source of the uid, and dropping the user namespace. For each it records the systemd-analyze exposure score against M5's and whether every target's systemd supports it. It also checks which SASL mechanism zbus offers as a peer-to-peer server so that identity comes only from the kernel (ANONYMOUS versus EXTERNAL). Ends with a 'Decision: ' line naming the route and the mechanism. If no route keeps the exposure score, the feature writes BLOCKED.md as SPEC says. Indexed in docs/findings.md.

features.title: Per-connection peer check, peer-to-peer D-Bus on the socket, and ListKeys for the peer's own uid

The D-Bus handshake uses a mechanism under which identity comes only from the kernel (F170), recorded in docs/decisions.md. An accepted peer gets the interface at the same name and path, and ListKeys returns only its uid's keys. Tests supply the label through a test-only source that never ships; a check run in `just quick` counts that nothing in data/ or packaging/ enables it (acceptance 15), with its test scripts/test-check-test-label.sh.
